stem: A team has a project containing a valid `tsconfig.json` file in the project root. A developer runs `tsc src/index.ts` from that root directory. Why does TypeScript report unexpected errors or ignore settings defined in `tsconfig.json`?
options: A tsconfig.json file can only be detected when input files are provided through stdin.
TypeScript only parses tsconfig.json if the command is executed with sudo or administrator privileges.
The compiler requires passing the -p flag whenever an individual file is located inside a subdirectory.
Passing input files directly on the command line causes tsc to ignore tsconfig.json configuration files.
objective: Write a tsconfig.json file enabling strict mode and project compilation

stem: You need to compile modern TypeScript code so that the emitted JavaScript runs on an environment that only supports ECMAScript 2015. Which configuration option achieves this downleveling in `tsconfig.json`?
objective: Configure the target compiler option to downlevel modern JavaScript syntax to ECMAScript 2015

stem: What is the effect of configuring `"strict": true` inside `compilerOptions` in a `tsconfig.json` file?
options: It restricts TypeScript to running only on ECMAScript 3 compatible runtime environments.
It forbids importing modules from external packages outside the local directory.
It activates all strict mode family options at once to provide stronger guarantees of program correctness.
It prevents JavaScript files from being emitted whenever any warning occurs during compilation.
objective: Write a tsconfig.json file enabling strict mode and project compilation
